mainTopic: The punishment and martyrdom of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון and the rescue of his daughter
overview: The amud begins by explaining why רבי חנינא בן תרדיון was punished: he pronounced God's Name as it is spelled. The גמרא asks how he could, since אבא שאול says such a person loses עולם הבא. It answers that he did it only to learn, and that his real sin was doing it in public. It then gives the reasons for his wife's punishment (she did not protest) and his daughter's (she enjoyed being admired for her walk), and all three accept God's judgment with פסוקים. Next a ברייתא tells how רבי יוסי בן קיסמא warned רבי חנינא not to teach תורה publicly against Rome's decree. The Romans later burned רבי חנינא wrapped in his ספר תורה. He saw the letters flying upward and refused to hasten his own death. The executioner sped up his death, jumped into the fire, and a בת קול announced that both would enter עולם הבא. Finally ברוריה asks רבי מאיר to rescue her sister. He tests her, bribes the guard, and teaches him to say 'אלהא דמאיר ענני'. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He pronounced God's Name as it is spelled
steps.stepSummary: The reason for רבי חנינא בן תרדיון's punishment: he pronounced the שם המפורש with its actual letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would pronounce God's special Name exactly as it is written.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the reason just given for why רבי חנינא בן תרדיון was sentenced to burning. It also sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the שם המפורש is not said the way it is spelled. The claim that רבי חנינא בן תרדיון did so is the basis for his punishment, and the גמרא will now question it.

keyTerms.meaning: with its letters, exactly as spelled

phrases.english: he would pronounce the Name with its letters.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון was punished for pronouncing the שם המפורש as it is spelled.

steps.title: How could a great צדיק do something that costs עולם הבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a משנה says, according to אבא שאול, that one who pronounces the Name as spelled has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do that? We learned in a משנה: These have no share in the World to Come: one who says the Torah is not from Heaven, and one who says תחיית המתים is not from the Torah. אבא שאול says: also one who pronounces the Name with its letters!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא בן תרדיון could do such a serious sin. It quotes a משנה to show how severe it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אבא שאול, pronouncing the Name as spelled is so bad that the person loses עולם הבא. It is hard to believe a great צדיק like רבי חנינא בן תרדיון would do that.

keyTerms.meaning: a share in the World to Come
the dead coming back to life

phrases.english: And how could he do that?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא —
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: These are the ones who have no share in the World to Come —
one who says the Torah is not from Heaven,
or that the resurrection of the dead is not from the Torah.
Abba Shaul says:
Also one who pronounces the Name with its letters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חנינא בן תרדיון pronounced the Name as spelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבא שאול in the משנה says this sin costs a person עולם הבא, so a צדיק would not do it.

steps.title: He did it only to learn
steps.stepSummary: He pronounced the Name only to learn it, and learning in order to understand is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did it to learn. As a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not learn to do' — but you may learn in order to understand and to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא בן תרדיון was not doing a forbidden act; he was studying. It brings a ברייתא showing that learning to understand is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids learning in order to DO forbidden things. Learning in order to understand and teach is permitted, so his saying the Name for study was not the sin אבא שאול meant.

keyTerms.meaning: to understand and to teach (or rule)

phrases.english: He did it to teach himself,
as it is taught: "You shall not learn to do",
but you may learn in order to understand and to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the forbidden act to doing, not studying.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any saying of the Name as spelled is the sin that costs עולם הבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying it to learn and understand is allowed, so רבי חנינא בן תרדיון did nothing wrong in that way.

steps.title: Then why was he punished?
steps.stepSummary: If studying was allowed, the גמרא asks what his sin really was.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason he was punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 3 removes the reason for his punishment, so the גמרא asks for a new reason. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once saying the Name to learn is allowed, there must be something else that made him deserve punishment.

phrases.english: Rather, what is the reason he was punished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 3, which left his punishment unexplained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real sin of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון.

steps.title: He said the Name in public
steps.stepSummary: His sin was pronouncing the Name in public instead of in private.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would pronounce the Name in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that his mistake was doing it openly, in front of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Studying the Name is fine in private. Saying it in public goes beyond study, and that is why he was punished.

phrases.english: Because he would pronounce the Name
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: in public,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהוֹגֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was punished for saying the Name in public.
steps.whatToRemember: Saying the Name to learn was allowed; doing it in public was his sin.

steps.title: His wife was punished for not protesting
steps.stepSummary: His wife was sentenced to death because she did not protest, which teaches that whoever can protest and does not is punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his wife was sentenced to be killed because she did not protest to him. From here they said: anyone who is able to protest and does not protest is punished for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why his wife was also punished. It then draws a general lesson about the duty to protest wrongdoing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She did not commit the sin herself, but she could have objected and stayed silent. From this the חכמים learn that one who is able to stop a sin and does not is punished along with the sinner.

phrases.english: And his wife was sentenced to be killed
because she did not protest against him.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Anyone who has the ability to protest
and does not protest is punished for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל אִשְׁתּוֹ לַהֲרִיגָה דְּלָא מַחַתָה בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 5: since his sin was public, she could have protested.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She was punished for not protesting his sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a lasting rule: one who can stop a wrong and stays silent shares in the punishment.

steps.title: His daughter enjoyed being admired for her walk
steps.stepSummary: His daughter was sentenced to a brothel because she began walking carefully to please the Roman nobles who praised her steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was his daughter sentenced to sit in a house of prostitutes? Because רבי יוחנן said: Once his daughter was walking before the nobles of Rome. They said: How pleasant are the steps of this girl! Right away she took care with her steps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the daughter's punishment with a story told by רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she heard the nobles praise her walk, she began walking in a way that would keep pleasing them. This seemingly small act of vanity is given as the reason for her harsh sentence.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל בִּתּוֹ לֵישֵׁב בְּקוּבָּה שֶׁל זוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: And his daughter, sentenced to sit in a brothel,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
Once his daughter was walking
before the nobles of Rome, and they said:

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה נָאוֹת פְּסִיעוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל רִיבָה זוֹ,
phrases.english: How pleasant are the steps of this young woman!
Immediately she took care with her steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל בִּתּוֹ לֵישֵׁב בְּקוּבָּה שֶׁל זוֹנוֹת, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the father and wife, the גמרא explains the third family member's punishment.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She was punished for walking in a way that would please the Roman nobles.

steps.title: Small sins trampled underfoot come back on the Day of Judgment
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's teaching on the פסוק 'עון עקבי יסובני' matches the daughter's story: sins a person treats as minor surround him at judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: What is the meaning of 'The sin of my heels surrounds me'? Sins that a person tramples with his heels in this world surround him on the Day of Judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the daughter's story to ריש לקיש's explanation of a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Trampling with one's heels' means treating a sin as unimportant. The daughter's walk seemed like a tiny thing, yet it counted heavily against her, just as ריש לקיש teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is the same as

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
What is meant by what is written: "The iniquity of my heels surrounds me"?

phrases.aramaic: עֲוֹנוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: Sins that a person tramples with his heels in this world
surround him on the Day of Judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the story in step 7 with a teaching on a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a small-seeming act like the daughter's walk can bring serious punishment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's explanation of 'עון עקבי יסובני' (תהלים 49:6).
steps.whatToRemember: Each family member's punishment had a reason: the father said the Name in public, the wife did not protest, and the daughter took pleasure in being admired. Sins that seem small still count.

steps.title: The three family members accept God's judgment with פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: As they leave after the sentencing, רבי חנינא בן תרדיון, his wife and his daughter each say a פסוק declaring that God's judgment is fair.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the three of them went out after being sentenced, they accepted that God's judgment was fair. He said: 'The Rock, His work is perfect.' His wife said: 'A God of faithfulness and without iniquity.' His daughter said: 'Great in counsel and mighty in work, whose eyes are open upon all the ways.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. Each of the three people sentenced in the earlier steps responds by saying a פסוק that calls God's judgment fair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 5 through 7, the גמרא gave each of them a sin that explains their punishment. Now they themselves admit the judgment is just. Each פסוק fits its speaker, and the daughter's פסוק, about God seeing all of a person's ways, connects to her sin of how she walked.

keyTerms.meaning: They accepted the judgment on themselves as fair
The Rock (God), His work is perfect
A faithful God, with no wrongdoing

phrases.english: When the three of them went out,
they accepted the judgment upon themselves as just.
He said: "The Rock, His work is perfect, etc."
And his wife said: "A God of faithfulness and without iniquity."
His daughter said: "Great in counsel and mighty in work,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר עֵינֶיךָ פְקֻחוֹת עַל כׇּל דַּרְכֵי וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: whose eyes are open upon all the ways, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיָּצְאוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּן, צִדְּקוּ עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the three sentences explained in steps 5 through 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three openly declared God's judgment to be just.

steps.title: רבי praises the family for finding the right פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי marvels that these righteous people thought of three fitting פסוקים of צידוק הדין at the very moment they needed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: How great are these righteous people, that three פסוקים about accepting God's judgment came to them at the very time they were accepting His judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי comments on the scene in step 9 and praises the family's greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What impresses רבי is not only that they accepted the judgment. It is that at a moment of terrible pain, the exact right פסוק came to each of them. He sees this as a sign of how righteous they were.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to them, happened to them at the right moment

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי treats the family's response as a model: at a moment of judgment, they found words declaring God's judgment just.

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
How great are these righteous people,
that three verses came to them

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל צִדּוּק הַדִּין בִּשְׁעַת צִדּוּק הַדִּין.
phrases.english: about accepting the judgment, at the time of accepting the judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: כַּמָּה גְּדוֹלִים צַדִּיקִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the three פסוקים quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their righteousness showed in finding fitting פסוקים of צידוק הדין at the moment of judgment.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא warns רבי חנינא בן תרדיון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: when רבי יוסי בן קיסמא is sick, he tells his visitor רבי חנינא בן תרדיון that Rome rules by Heaven's decree, so teaching תורה in public is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When רבי יוסי בן קיסמא fell ill, רבי חנינא בן תרדיון went to visit him. He said to him: Chanina my brother, don't you know that this nation was made to rule by Heaven? It destroyed God's House, burned His Sanctuary, killed His pious ones and destroyed His best ones, and it still stands. And I heard that you sit and learn תורה, gather crowds in public, and keep a ספר תורה in your lap!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with more of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון's story. It opens with רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's reasoning is that if Rome could destroy the בית המקדש and still survive, Heaven must have given it power. So openly defying its ban on teaching תורה seems reckless. This sets up the coming exchange about רבי חנינא's fate.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma fell ill,

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן לְבַקְּרוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon went to visit him.
He said to him: Chanina my brother,
phrases.notes: Some versions say "my brother" twice; the corrected wording leaves out the second one, in round brackets.

phrases.english: don't you know that this nation
was given its rule by Heaven?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֶחְרִיבָה אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְשָׂרְפָה אֶת הֵיכָלוֹ,
phrases.english: For it destroyed His House and burned His Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרְגָה אֶת חֲסִידָיו וְאִבְּדָה אֶת טוֹבָיו,
phrases.english: and killed His pious ones and destroyed His best ones,
and it still exists.
And I heard about you
that you sit and engage in Torah,
and gather crowds in public,
and have a scroll lying in your lap!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִיסְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the same רבי חנינא בן תרדיון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since Rome rules by Heaven's decree, openly teaching תורה against its ban puts one in danger.

steps.title: רבי חנינא answers that Heaven will have mercy
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון answers the warning by trusting that Heaven will protect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Heaven will have mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא responds to the warning in step 11 by expressing trust in God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with the political reasoning. He simply relies on Heaven's mercy to protect him while he keeps teaching.

phrases.english: He said to him: Heaven will have mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's warning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He trusts that Heaven will protect him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא rejects the answer and predicts burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא objects that relying on mercy doesn't answer his reasoning, and he predicts that רבי חנינא and his ספר תורה will be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am telling you sensible things, and you answer me 'Heaven will have mercy'? I would be amazed if they don't burn you and the ספר תורה in fire!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא pushes back on the answer in step 12 and warns about what will happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues that a reasoned warning needs a reasoned response, not just hope for mercy. His prediction points ahead to how רבי חנינא בן תרדיון was actually killed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי אוֹמֵר לְךָ דְּבָרִים שֶׁל טַעַם,
phrases.english: He said to him: I am telling you sensible things,
and you say to me "Heaven will have mercy"?
I would be amazed

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא יִשְׂרְפוּ אוֹתְךָ וְאֶת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בָּאֵשׁ!
phrases.english: if they do not burn you and the Torah scroll in fire!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי אוֹמֵר לְךָ דְּבָרִים שֶׁל טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חנינא's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's reliance on 'Heaven will have mercy'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hoping for mercy does not answer the clear danger shown by Rome's Heaven-given power.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks about his share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: Hearing that he may die, רבי חנינא בן תרדיון asks whether he is fit for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, what about me? Am I destined for the life of עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא turns the conversation to his own spiritual standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since death seems likely, his real worry is no longer this world. He wants to know whether he has earned עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Life in the World to Come

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
what am I for the life of the World to Come?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי, מָה אֲנִי לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the prediction of his death.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether he has a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא asks about a special deed
steps.stepSummary: Before answering, רבי יוסי בן קיסמא asks whether any special deed has come to רבי חנינא's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Has any special deed come your way?
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering right away, רבי יוסי בן קיסמא asks a question back to find out what his answer should be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He looks for one meaningful act that would show רבי חנינא's standing. This sets up the story in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Did any deed come to your hand?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּלוּם מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לְיָדֶךָ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did any deed come to your hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question back before answering step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A specific deed that would show רבי חנינא's merit.

steps.title: The mixed-up פורים money
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא tells how his own פורים money got mixed up with צדקה money, and he gave all of it to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My money for פורים got mixed up with צדקה money, and I gave all of it out to the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question from step 15 with a story about himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He could not tell which coins were his own, so rather than risk keeping צדקה money, he gave everything to the poor at his own cost. This is the merit the conversation was looking for.

phrases.english: He said to him:
My Purim money got mixed up for me
with charity money,
and I distributed them to the poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He gave his own mixed-up פורים money to the poor along with the צדקה money.

steps.title: May my portion be like yours
steps.stepSummary: Hearing the story, רבי יוסי בן קיסמא prays that his own portion and lot be like רבי חנינא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, may my portion be from your portion, and may my lot be from your lot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא ends the conversation by showing how great he thinks רבי חנינא's standing is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He answers the question about עולם הבא without stating it directly. By wishing to share רבי חנינא's fate, he shows that רבי חנינא surely has a share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: May my portion be from your portion

steps.whatToRemember: Even after warning רבי חנינא בן תרדיון of danger, רבי יוסי בן קיסמא ends by wishing to share his fate, because of his honesty with צדקה money.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
may my portion be from your portion,
and may my lot be from your lot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the story in step 16 and answers the question from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון's merit is so great that רבי יוסי בן קיסמא wishes to share his portion.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא dies and רבי חנינא is found teaching in public
steps.stepSummary: A few days later רבי יוסי בן קיסמא dies and is honored by the Roman leaders. On their way back they find רבי חנינא בן תרדיון teaching תורה in public with a ספר תורה in his lap.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: only a few days passed before רבי יוסי בן קיסמא died. All the great men of Rome went to bury him and gave him a great eulogy. On their way back, they found רבי חנינא בן תרדיון sitting and learning תורה, gathering crowds in public, with a ספר תורה resting in his lap.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The Romans honor רבי יוסי at his funeral, and then they catch רבי חנינא doing exactly what רבי יוסי warned him not to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast is sharp. רבי יוסי got along with the Romans, so they honored him even in death. רבי חנינא kept teaching openly in defiance of the decree, and this sets up the fulfillment of רבי יוסי's prediction from Step 13.

phrases.english: They said: not even a few days passed

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁנִּפְטַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִיסְמָא,
phrases.english: before Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma died,
and all the great men of Rome went to bury him
and they eulogized him with a great eulogy.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַחֲזָרָתָן מְצָאוּהוּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן
phrases.english: And on their way back they found Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon
sitting and learning Torah
and gathering crowds in public
with a Torah scroll resting in his lap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's prayer, moving to the fulfillment of his prediction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי dies in honor, and רבי חנינא is caught teaching תורה in public.

steps.title: רבי חנינא is burned wrapped in the ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The Romans wrap רבי חנינא in the ספר תורה and set him on fire. They put wet wool on his heart so that he would die slowly.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him, wrapped him in the ספר תורה, surrounded him with bundles of branches, and set them on fire. They brought tufts of wool, soaked them in water, and put them on his heart so that his soul would not leave quickly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי's prediction comes true exactly: רבי חנינא and his ספר תורה are burned together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wet wool shows how cruel the punishment was, because it was meant to make the suffering last longer. This detail sets up the later conversations about whether he should speed up his own death.
steps.confusionAlert: The wet wool was not meant to help him. It was there to keep him alive longer so that he would suffer more.

phrases.english: They brought him and wrapped him in the Torah scroll,
and surrounded him with bundles of branches
and set them on fire,
and they brought tufts of wool
and soaked them in water and put them on his heart,
so that his soul would not leave quickly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the punishment that follows his arrest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא is burned with the ספר תורה, and his death is deliberately slowed.

steps.title: His daughter cries out at seeing him this way
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא's daughter asks in pain how she can see her father like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: His daughter said to him: Father, must I see you like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter cries out in pain, and this sets up רבי חנינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is phrased as a question, but it is really a cry of grief. It gives רבי חנינא the chance to explain why he is at peace.

keyTerms.meaning: must I see you like this?

phrases.english: His daughter said to him:
Father, must I see you like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the burning described in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can she bear to see her father suffering like this?

steps.title: He is comforted because the ספר תורה burns with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says that burning alone would have been hard. But since the ספר תורה burns with him, ה׳, who will avenge the insult to the תורה, will also avenge his insult.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: If I were being burned alone, it would be hard for me. Now that I am burning together with a ספר תורה, the One who will demand justice for the insult to the ספר תורה will also demand justice for the insult to me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא comforts his daughter. Being burned together with the ספר תורה ties his fate to the honor of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The very thing the Romans did to shame him turns into his comfort. Because his suffering is joined to the תורה's suffering, ה׳'s response to the insult against the תורה will include him.

keyTerms.meaning: will seek, will demand justice for

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: אִילְמָלֵי אֲנִי נִשְׂרַפְתִּי לְבַדִּי
phrases.english: He said to her: If I were being burned alone,
the matter would be hard for me;

phrases.aramaic: עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאֲנִי נִשְׂרָף וְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה עִמִּי,
phrases.english: now that I am burning and a Torah scroll is with me,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁמְבַקֵּשׁ עֶלְבּוֹנָהּ שֶׁל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: the One who seeks justice for the insult to the Torah scroll
He will seek justice for my insult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: אִילְמָלֵי אֲנִי נִשְׂרַפְתִּי לְבַדִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers his daughter's cry.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His suffering is bound up with the ספר תורה, so ה׳ will avenge him together with the תורה.

steps.title: His students ask what he sees
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא's students ask him what he is seeing as he burns.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, what do you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a question, and this sets up his famous answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students sense that their teacher, at this moment, may be seeing something beyond the physical fire.

phrases.english: His students said to him:
Rebbi, what do you see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new speaker, his students, addresses him during the burning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי חנינא seeing at this moment?

steps.title: The parchment burns but the letters fly upward
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that the parchment is burning, but the letters are flying away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The parchment is burning, and the letters are flying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא describes what he sees: only the physical parchment is destroyed, while the letters of the תורה rise up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Romans can burn the material scroll, but they cannot destroy the תורה itself. The holy letters survive and fly away.
steps.whatToRemember: גווילין נשרפין ואותיות פורחות: the parchment can be burned, but the תורה itself cannot be destroyed.

phrases.english: He said to them: the parchments are burning
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has גליון in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, reads גווילין, "parchments."

phrases.english: and the letters are flying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: גְּוִילִין נִשְׂרָפִין וְאוֹתִיּוֹת פּוֹרְחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The parchment burns, but the letters fly away and are not destroyed.

steps.title: The students urge him to open his mouth and end the suffering
steps.stepSummary: The students suggest that he open his mouth so the fire enters and he dies quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: You too, open your mouth so the fire will enter you.
steps.whatsHappening: The students offer a way for him to end his suffering faster, and this sets up his refusal in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the wet wool was slowing his death, the students propose that he speed it up himself. This raises the question of whether a person may hasten his own death.

keyTerms.meaning: and the fire will enter you

phrases.english: You too, open your mouth
and the fire will enter you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The students follow up with a practical suggestion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students propose that he hasten his death to end the pain.

steps.title: He refuses: only the One who gave life may take it
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא refuses. It is better that ה׳, who gave the soul, take it, and a person should not harm himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is better that the One who gave it should take it, and a person should not harm himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא turns down the suggestion, even though it would end his pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's soul belongs to ה׳, so a person may not actively hurt himself to speed up his death. Even in terrible suffering, רבי חנינא will not take that step himself.

keyTerms.meaning: that the One who gave it should take it

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is a well-known source for the idea that a person may not actively shorten his own life, even when he is suffering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: מוּטָב שֶׁיִּטְּלֶנָּה מִי שֶׁנְּתָנָהּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: It is better that the One who gave it should take it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the soul, and "the One who gave it" is ה׳.

phrases.english: and a person should not harm himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: מוּטָב שֶׁיִּטְּלֶנָּה מִי שֶׁנְּתָנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the students' suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only ה׳ may take the soul, and a person must not hurt himself to hasten death.

steps.title: The executioner offers to speed his death in exchange for עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The executioner asks whether, if he raises the flame and removes the wool, רבי חנינא will bring him to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The executioner said to him: רבי, if I make the flame bigger and take the tufts of wool off your heart, will you bring me to the life of עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: A new speaker, the Roman executioner, makes an offer and asks for a promise in return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא refused to harm himself, but here someone else offers to hasten his death. The executioner wants a reward for it: a share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: the life of the World to Come

phrases.english: The executioner said to him: Rebbi,
if I make the flame bigger

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹטֵל סְפוֹגִין שֶׁל צֶמֶר מֵעַל לִבְּךָ,
phrases.english: and take the tufts of wool off your heart,
will you bring me to the life of the World to Come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי חנינא refuses to hasten his own death, an outsider offers to do it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Will רבי חנינא guarantee the executioner עולם הבא if he ends the suffering?

steps.title: רבי חנינא agrees and swears
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says yes. The executioner asks him to swear, and he swears.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. The executioner said: Swear to me. He swore to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא accepts the offer and backs it up with an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא would not hurt himself, but he agrees when someone else does the act. The oath makes the promise of עולם הבא firm.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
"Swear to me." He swore to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the executioner's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, and he confirms it with an oath.

steps.title: רבי חנינא dies quickly and the executioner jumps into the fire
steps.stepSummary: The executioner raises the flame and removes the wool, and רבי חנינא dies quickly. The executioner then jumps into the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately he made the flame bigger and took the tufts of wool off his heart, and his soul left quickly. Then he too jumped and fell into the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The executioner keeps his side of the deal, and רבי חנינא's suffering ends. Then the executioner throws himself into the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The executioner's leap shows how fully he committed himself to his choice. This sets up what the story says next about his reward.

phrases.english: Immediately he made the flame bigger

phrases.aramaic: וְנָטַל סְפוֹגִין שֶׁל צֶמֶר מֵעַל לִבּוֹ,
phrases.english: and took the tufts of wool off his heart,
and his soul left quickly.

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא קָפַץ וְנָפַל לְתוֹךְ הָאוּר.
phrases.english: He too jumped and fell into the fire.
phrases.notes: "He" here is the executioner, not רבי חנינא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the deal made in Steps 26 and 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא dies quickly, and the executioner gives up his own life in the fire.

steps.title: A heavenly voice announces both men's reward
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול declares that רבי חנינא בן תרדיון and the executioner are both ready for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון and the executioner are both ready for the life of the World-to-Come.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers the executioner's question from step 26. His deal with רבי חנינא, sealed with an oath in step 27, was accepted, and both men go to עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 ended with רבי חנינא swearing that the executioner would get עולם הבא. Here a בת קול confirms that the promise came true. The executioner is named right next to the great צדיק.

phrases.english: A Divine Voice came out and said:
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Teradyon and the executioner
are ready for the life of the World-to-Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the heavenly result of the executioner's act and his jump into the fire
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי חנינא בן תרדיון and the executioner merit עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי cries over earning a world in one moment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא cries. Some people earn עולם הבא in one moment, and others only after many years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי cried and said: Some people earn their World-to-Come in one moment, and some earn it only after many years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי draws the lesson of the whole story. The executioner earned in one moment what רבי חנינא earned through a lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The executioner did one great act and earned עולם הבא at once. רבי חנינא earned the same through many years of תורה and מסירות נפש. רבי is moved to tears that one moment can count so much.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquires his world, meaning he earns his share in עולם הבא

steps.whatToRemember: A single moment of doing the right thing can earn a person עולם הבא, just like a whole lifetime of good deeds.

phrases.english: Rebbi cried and said:
phrases.notes: When the גמרא just says 'רבי', it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: There is one who acquires his world in one moment,
and there is one who acquires his world only after many years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a moral from the בת קול's announcement
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולם הבא can be earned in one moment, or through many years of effort.

steps.title: ברוריה asks רבי מאיר to save her sister
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. ברוריה, the daughter of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון, tells רבי מאיר it shames her that her sister is in a house of prostitutes.
steps.simpleTranslation: ברוריה, the wife of רבי מאיר, was a daughter of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון. She said to him: It is shameful for me that my sister is sitting in a house of prostitutes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story about the family of רבי חנינא. This line sets up the rescue that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on this daf, the Romans punished רבי חנינא's daughter by sending her to a house of prostitutes. Now her sister ברוריה pushes her husband to act. Her words hint that he must rescue her.

keyTerms.meaning: ברוריה, the learned wife of רבי מאיר
It is a shameful thing for me

phrases.english: Berurya, the wife of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַתֵּיה דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: was a daughter of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Teradyon.
She said to him:
It is a shameful thing for me
that my sister is sitting in a house of prostitutes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about רבי חנינא's family
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברוריה asks רבי מאיר to rescue her sister.

steps.title: רבי מאיר sets a test before going
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר takes a container of dinars and goes. He decides that a miracle will happen only if she has not sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took a container full of dinars and went. He said: If she did not sin, a miracle will happen for her. If she sinned, no miracle will happen for her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר brings money for the rescue. He also decides that a miracle will help only if the sister stayed pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money is meant for paying off the guards. רבי מאיר knows the rescue will need help from Heaven. He believes that help will come only if she did not sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A container (a measure) full of dinars

phrases.english: He took a container full of dinars and went.
He said to himself:
If no sin was done with her,
a miracle will happen;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'will happen.'

phrases.english: if she did sin,
no miracle will happen for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי מאיר responds to ברוריה's request
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miracle will come only if the sister has stayed pure.

steps.title: רבי מאיר tests the sister in disguise
steps.stepSummary: Dressed as a Roman horseman, רבי מאיר asks her to sin. She pushes him off with excuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He dressed up as a Roman horseman and said to her: Give in to me. She said: I am a נדה. He said: I will wait. She said: There are many women here who are prettier than me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר checks for himself whether she has stayed pure. He pretends to be a customer, and she keeps refusing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time he answers her excuse, she comes up with a new one. First she says she is a נדה. When he says he will wait, she points him to other women.

keyTerms.meaning: Listen to me, meaning give in to my wishes
A woman who is a נדה

phrases.english: He went and made himself look like a Roman horseman.
He said to her: Give in to me.
She said to him: I am a niddah.
He said to her: I will wait.
She said to him: There are many women
(and there are many here) who are prettier than me.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't; the point is the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the check on whether she sinned
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sister refuses the disguised רבי מאיר with excuses.

steps.title: רבי מאיר concludes she stayed pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר decides that she must give every visitor these excuses, so she has not sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I can learn from this that she has not sinned. She must say this to everyone who comes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר draws his conclusion from the test. Her ready excuses show she uses them on everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Excuses this smooth are not a one-time thing. They show a steady habit of protecting herself. So he concludes she has stayed pure, and the rescue can go ahead.

phrases.english: He said to himself: Learn from this
that she has not sinned;
she says this to everyone who comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לָא עֲבַדָה אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the test in step 33
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sister has stayed pure, so she deserves a miracle.

steps.title: The guard is afraid to release her
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר asks the guard to hand her over. The guard says he fears the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to her guard and said: Give her to me. The guard said: I am afraid of the government.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר moves on to freeing her. The guard raises a problem: he will be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that he knows she is pure, רבי מאיר tries to get her out. The guard's fear sets up רבי מאיר's offer in the next step.

phrases.english: He went to her guard.
He said to him: Give her to me.
The guard said to him: I am afraid of the government.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from testing her to freeing her
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guard refuses because he fears punishment.

steps.title: רבי מאיר offers money as a bribe
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר gives the guard the dinars. Half is for bribing the officials, and half is for the guard to keep.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Take this container of dinars. Give half as a bribe, and half will be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers the guard's fear with money. The bribe can protect him, and he also gets paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying off the officials takes care of the danger, and the other half makes the deal worth it for the guard. This is the money רבי מאיר brought in step 32.

phrases.english: He said to him: Take this container of dinars;
give half as a bribe,
and half will be for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the guard's fear
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bribe money will protect the guard, with extra left for himself.

steps.title: The guard asks what happens when the money runs out
steps.stepSummary: The guard worries that once the money is gone, he will have nothing left to save himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The guard said: And when the money runs out, what will I do?
steps.whatsHappening: The guard raises a new worry. The money will not last forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money solves the problem only for a while. The guard wants to know how he will be protected after that. This sets up רבי מאיר's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: They run out, they are used up

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי שָׁלְמִי מַאי אֶיעְבֵּיד?
phrases.english: He said to him: And when the money runs out, what will I do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the money offered in step 36 will not last
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How will the guard be protected after the money is gone?

steps.title: Say 'God of Meir, answer me'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר tells the guard to say 'אלהא דמאיר ענני' and he will be saved. The guard starts to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Say 'God of Meir, answer me!' and you will be saved. The guard said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives the guard a prayer to say when he is in danger. The last words open the guard's reply, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the money is gone, the guard will need protection from Heaven. רבי מאיר promises that saying these words will save him. The guard's response is just beginning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the well-known prayer 'אלהא דמאיר ענני'.

phrases.english: He said to him: Say: 'God of Meir, answer me!'
